name: Labor
overview: Scripture presents labor as a divinely ordained responsibility beginning with God's placement of man in the garden to work and keep it (Genesis 2:15). Following the Fall, work is associated with toil and effort, as reflected in the necessity to eat bread by the sweat of one's face (Genesis 3:19). The Mosaic Law further structures labor by commanding six days of work followed by a Sabbath rest, emphasizing both diligent work and the need for rest for all, including servants and animals (Exodus 20:9-11; 23:12). This balance highlights God's design for labor as purposeful and ordered within His creation.
